_readme: Real US macro releases used by the transmission study (src/research/transmission.mjs).
Figures are transcribed from the public releases (BLS CPI, BLS employment situation,
FOMC statements). `side` is derived mechanically as sign(actual - consensus) at run time,
never hand-picked, so the study cannot be tuned to its own answer.
Realised prices come from data/prices/*.csv (see scripts/fetch-prices.mjs for provenance).
`polarity` is +1 unless stated. It encodes whether a HIGHER number means a HOTTER
surprise. Only metrics whose natural direction is inverted (e.g. projected rate CUTS)
carry -1. Polarity is declared up front from the metric definition, not fitted.
If you spot a transcription error, fix it here and re-run: node scripts/replay.mjs

events.label: FOMC +75bp
events.note: Consensus is the market's expectation ON THE DAY. Fed funds futures had fully repriced to 75bp by 2022-06-13, so the decision itself was not a surprise and the study correctly skips it.

events.label: SVB failure - credit shock
events.note: Risk-off control event: flight to duration, not an inflation print.

events.label: CPI y/y (Jun 2024)
events.note: Cool print but mega-cap growth fell anyway - the great rotation. Kept as an honest failure case.

events.label: FOMC 2025 easing projections
events.note: The 25bp cut itself was fully expected. The surprise was the dot plot halving projected 2025 easing. FEWER projected cuts = HAWKISH, hence polarity -1.

events.label: Core CPI y/y (Dec 2024)
events.note: Headline CPI was in line at 2.9%; the tradeable surprise was core at 3.2% vs 3.3% expected, which is what drove the rally.

events.label: Reciprocal tariff pause
events.note: 90-day pause announcement - the largest one-day risk-on dispersion in the sample.

events.label: Nonfarm payrolls (Jul)
events.note: Weak print plus large downward revisions to May and June.

events.label: CPI y/y (Aug 2025)
events.note: Headline cool, core 3.1% vs 3.0% hot - a genuinely two-sided print.
